article.title: Melat Kiros
article.author: Ann Garrison
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. On November 11th, Colorado’s First-District Congresswoman-elect Melat Kiros, who represents Denver, joined seven other newly elected members in voting against uber Zionist and corporatist Hakeem Jeffries to lead the Democratic Party in the House. Just two days later, the Denverite published “ Melat Kiros may face a notable Democratic challenger in 2028 ,” an announcement that establishment Democrat Crisanta Duran had formed an exploratory committee to consider a run against Kiros back in September, two months before voters had even gone to the polls. The emerging Democratic Party’s civil war will soon be in full force and getting uglier than it already has. The Clinton-Obama moderates, who aren't really moderate at all, are already trying to take back what they lost to the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), including Melat Kiros and five more Congressional electeds on November 3. Another anti-war, anti-Zionist advocate for Medicare-for-All, Ohio’s Don Leonard, also says he wants a Constitutional Amendment to overturn Citizens United, the Supreme Court decision that opened the floodgates to special interest money controlling US elections. The “moderates” who have hold of the levers of power no doubt hate these young new, non-white DSA members of Congress even more than they despise MAGA. Why? Because, for one, should they stick to DSA’s espoused principles, they could make faux progressive members of Congress look bad, as they just did in the vote for Speaker. Related: Rwanda's Transnational Prosecutions and Narrative Grip Note, however, that they also made two of their own, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Rashida Tlaib, look bad. What kind of socialist or even progressive votes to so hugely empower a Black man who, in 2014, spoke to over 10,000 people at a “New York Stands with Israel” rally during Israel’s Operation Protective Edge massacres in Gaza. A Black man who kept chanting variations of, “Israel today, Israel tomorrow, Israel Forever!”, echoing the late Alabama Governor George Wallace’s rallying cry, “Segregation today, segregation tomorrow, segregation forever!” Who said that Israel lived in a tough neighborhood where it should not apologize for its strength, then joined in the next ten years of hostilities that led to the US-Israeli War on Iran, while taking more than $1.7 million in AIPAC donations and affirming his devotion at the Wailing Wall in Jerusalem? The incoming DSA electeds exposed those two already there, along with all the other faux progressives who have no red lines, not even genocide. And how did DSA respond? As soon as the votes were counted, New York DSA held a national Zoom to draft AOC for president. Even on the outside, they would seem to have no red lines either. In 2024, AOC joined fellow progressives in, they said, opposing offensive weapons to Israel while supporting defensive systems like Iron Dome, and voted against Marjorie Taylor Greene's amendment to cut $500 million from the system because it left offensive aid untouched. In 2026, she made a big splash at a DSA conference by saying she now opposes all military aid to Israel because they can afford to pay for it themselves. (With US aid, or given that US taxpayers pick up so many of their bills for things like universal health insurance?) The Democratic Party slugfest is on despite the compliance of DSA’s biggest star and most likely presidential candidate with the Zionist agenda. Related: Navi Pillay’s Nobel Peace Prize and the Dark Legacy of the Rwanda Tribunal Democratic strategist James Carville, Bill Clinton’s 1992 campaign manager, was named Campaign Manager of the Year by the American Association of Political Consultants after helping Clinton beat George Herbert Walker Bush, but in October 2026, he said he would rather Republicans keep a five-seat House majority than have Democrats win by five seats and be "hostage to the DSA." He clearly treats them as a greater threat to his party than MAGA. The Democrats predictably won by closer to 40 seats, so it must have been those five DSA seats that Carville saw coming. Perhaps he fears that in a close vote with a lot of “moderates” voting with MAGA, the DSA voters could be a small but significant block. Establishment Democrats saw his coming Denver is a Democratic town, so Kiros won her seat back in June, when she upset Diane DeGette, a 15-term incumbent who had held onto the seat for 30 years. Kiros had never held political office though she did belong to the Denver chapter of DSA, and she had soared to prominence when she sacrificed her job by refusing to un-publish “ Dear US Law Firms ,” a Medium editorial responding to an open letter published by 100 major U.S. law firms (including her then-employer, Sidley Austin, LLP). The lawyers had urged law schools to take a strong stance against anti-Semitism and Islamophobia on campus and specifically treated “calls for the elimination of the Israeli state” as a form of anti-Semitism. Kiros responded that they were conflating criticism with anti-Semitism, that Israel had weaponized charges of anti-Semitism to defend apartheid, ethnic cleansing, and collective punishment against Palestinians. She cited human rights groups accusing Israel of apartheid and framed the conflict’s roots in the Balfour Declaration and British colonialism, the 1948 Nakba (which she pointed out involved mass killings and the displacement of hundreds of thousands of Palestinians), and ongoing restrictions on Palestinians. She also referenced statements by some Israeli officials that she viewed as genocidal in rhetoric regarding Gaza. She argued for a one-state solution with equal rights for all. That is quite a contrast to AOC, who went into Congress saying that she was no expert on Israel and Palestine. DSA Denver responded with an extraordinary organizing effort that drew in volunteers from around the country. Kiros upset DeGette, who outspent her by roughly $2 million overall, with much of the money pouring in near the end of the race when it was clear Kiros had taken the lead. Related: Ethiopia vs. Eritrea: A New War Could Send Oil and Gas Prices Soaring Similar contests are likely to shape up in the next two years, with DSA trying to out-organize and fundraise establishment Dems with corporate and oligarch money to burn. How many more millions would they be willing to spend to see whether someone as bland as Cristana Duran can take on Melat Kiros? Like AOC, Kiros is likely here to stay, but how will she and the others who dared say no to Jeffries vote in another two years? After their votes against Jeffries, they would probably be assigned to Dogcatching and Garbage Pickup Committees if they existed. There will no doubt be charges of anti-Semitism at every turn. They’re not likely to be given much to take home to their constituents in the way of jobs and civic improvements. DSA has changed the political landscape, and more battles are looming, but AOC’s rising star doesn’t promise radical change. It nevertheless seems only fair to let the six who voted no to “Israel today, tomorrow, and forever” take their seats and see what they can do. Black Agenda Report
